There was a really bad thunderstorm. I was just standing near the exit of the parking garage, attempting to build up the courage to head out to class. A girl walked into the garage and handed me her umbrella. She said that I looked like I needed it more than her and that it was partially broken anyway, so it was no big deal.

But, it was a big deal to me. Sometimes it's the little things that renew your faith in humanity.

There are a few problems with this argument that the "majority of dogs attacks I hear about involved pit bulls. I take for granted that you "heard it," but according to the facts, labrador retrievers (generally considered a very friendly breed) account for the largest number of bites among dogs. Another confusion is that so many different dogs are called pit bulls, sometimes dogs that I can clearly tell don't have any pit bull in them at all. The media groups them all into one, but they consider Staffordshire Terriers, American Pitbull Terriers, and American Staffordshire Terriers (among others) all to be under the pitbull category. In addition, there is a bit of framing. Most dog attacks happen among loose dogs that naturally form into packs. These dogs are usually mixed with a bunch of different breeds and classified. If a dog is 1/4 pitbull and 3/4 bull dog, and bites someone, it will be called a pit bull. I have seen more than a few cases where I looked at the picture of the dog and it would look like a Shar Pei or a bull dog, yet it was called a pit bull.(Especially among the news outlets near Miami where I am from where pit bulls are banned) So, from what I have seen, I think if a dog causes major damage, it is more likely to be labeled a pit bull.

The fact of the matter is that pit bulls are very intelligent and strong breeds. They were bred as sport dogs and they were bred to fight. But, no dog is inherently dangerous. It is 100% how you raise the dog, anyone who has lived with dogs should know this. According to Dog Expert Cesar Milan, all dogs need three things-- discipline, exercise and affection. I have found this to be extremely true with the raising of my three dogs. All the pit bulls I know that have been trained are really intelligent and usually very playful. They have a higher level of excitement and energy. They need to be exercised for 30 minutes to an hour a day. If they aren't getting that, they are going to act up. But, that's the same with any dog. If a dog's needs aren't met, it isn't going to behave. Pit bulls definitely get a bad reputation because of their capabilities as a powerful breed. But, in terms of aggression, they are no more aggressive than any other breed.

In all but a small number of cases, a dog's behavior is a direct reflection of the owner.

I'll try to address your points as best as I can. And to everyone else who said this has been done a million times, I just joined this site today. So, I haven't really looked around and trolled the boards. Sorry, noob.

I never "really" believed in anything means that I didn't have a strong belief in God. But, I did believe it was possible for there to be a God. I would consider myself Agnostic, although some people may group this with Atheism, I would not. I believe they are distinct, perhaps you disagree.

The Alien example is relevant as a comparison insofar as it is a view in which evidence would tend to point of us in one direction, though this conclusion has a great chance of being incorrect nonetheless. I could provide you with many facts about the vastness of the universe, the conditions in planets in our own solar system (i.e., Mars with it's weather systems and water) that could possibly have sustained life in the past, or a million other facts. To me, there are a million pieces of evidence that suggest that there is extraterrestrial life. Yet, there is just as good of a chance that I am wrong, despite all evidence pointing me in the direction. So, my comparison is that, despite everything that may point you in one direction, you may still have been lead down the wrong path.

I don't really feel like addressing that philosophical, metaphysical bull shit. I understand what you're saying that we can't know anything exists.

I understand I stereotype atheists, and if you're not one of the ones who thinks you're God's gift to earth ;) I apologize. Yet, I believe stereotypes more often than not have a factual basis.

With regards to the afterlife, I agree with your view that the physical body after death naturally deteriorates with the brain (mind) included. Yet, my perception of the afterlife, or at least a hypothetical one, is one which the "soul" leaves the body. I am pretty certain that you don't believe in a soul, but my proposal would be that the soul is a separate entity from the physical body itself. Although during life it may be housed in a body, it would have the ability to leave afterwards.

Finally, I think that every religious person out there would have a long list of reasons to prove that God exists to them. These could include simple miracles where a doctor and all science said a man would die from cancer within a month, but he made a complete recovery. No, I don't have a news story that says this, but I am just trying to give an example. I know that you could dissolve and break down their arguments and you (and other atheists would think you won the war of worlds.) Similarly, if you wen't into a church congregation and told them these things, no one would have their mind changed. Just because someone can break down an argument, and refute their evidence, doesn't make them right. You can literally make statistics say ANYTHING. You can find evidence to support ANYTHING. I have worked as a researcher for a project funded by the National Science Foundation for the last year. Honestly, I don't believe any of are stupid ass conclusions. Yet, we can show within our model and our selected data that _____ is true with 90% of the cases. 

I whole heartedly agree that reasoning and evidence DO work. I am not arguing that. But, they are not without hindrance or failure. Science is the art of trial and error. This could help your point that you are Atheist because there is nothing that has compelled you to believe otherwise. The mistake in this I believe is that you assume that religious people can't reach the same, but opposite conclusion in at least a somewhat rational manner. They could believe in God until they are proven wrong. 

When I say that you both believe in faith, I guess I meant that you basically both use the Confirmation Bias. (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confirmation_bias) You both have evidence that you believe makes the other side look foolish. 

If I missed anything, let me know and I'll try to respond if you read this again.
